verifiedBoundaryModel.finding: Core OBSERVES THE ADAPTER. The original EOA identity is consumed at the adapter hop.
proven: direct EOA -> Core: Core observes the EOA
Adapter -> Core via gl.get_contract_at + emit(on='accepted'): Core observes the ADAPTER
Adapter forwarding a spoofed JSON declared_source: Core still observes the ADAPTER, proving a JSON source field carries no provenance
unregistered adapter rejected by Core on sender address
adapter attempting to widen amount rejected by Core on a Core-side cap
verifiedBoundaryModel.consequence: No signed receipt or proof-carrying mechanism is required. Core authenticates the Adapter from gl.message.sender_address; the Adapter authenticates the adjudicator from the sender it observes.
verifiedBoundaryModel.notYetProvenLive: The spike ran on GLSim localnet. Bradbury caller semantics are re-proved as a gate below. Local spike semantics must NOT be promoted to live evidence.

architecture.Adjudicator: actual caller -> Adapter. Separate future contract; NOT built in this work.
architecture.Adapter: actual caller -> Core via emit(on='accepted'). Owns registry, origin binding, receipts, proposals. NO balance authority.
architecture.Core: final deterministic consequence boundary. Owns ledger, policy, attestation, capital, send gates, settlement. Balance mutates ONLY here.

adapterMandatoryGates: adjudicator registry (source_contract, authority_fingerprint, policy_version, status, created_at, expires_at)
source origin bound to the actual gl.message.sender_address of the caller, never to a JSON field
decision_id replay protection (consumed on first submission, actionable or not)
proposal construction and proposal_id replay protection
no balance authority of any kind
cannot bypass Core: every disposition must go through Core
coreMandatoryGates: adapter registry; the actual caller must be a registered, non-revoked, unexpired adapter
refusal returned as an OBSERVABLE STATUS, never as an unexplained revert
independent revalidation at execution time of: policy, recipient, amount, attestation, capital, replay, expiry, account status
balance mutation only after every Core gate passes
re-reads Core state at execution time and does NOT trust Adapter-supplied state or Adapter-supplied assertions about policy/limits

asynchronousBoundary.model: Adapter accepts -> emit(on='accepted') -> Core executes in a LATER transaction
asynchronousBoundary.atomicity: NON-ATOMIC. The boundary must be treated as non-atomic throughout.
asynchronousBoundary.consequence: Core must not trust Adapter state at execution time. Everything is re-read and revalidated by Core.
asynchronousBoundary.appealHazard: An Adapter transaction appealed after emit() does NOT automatically cancel Core execution; the emitted call still runs. Core-side validation is therefore the only mitigation and remains mandatory.
asynchronousBoundary.refusalSemantics: Core must not raise to signal refusal on an emitted call. Proven in the spike: a rejecting raise produced an absent artifact indistinguishable from 'the emit never landed'; the identical logic changed to return a verdict produced a readable verdict. Refusal is a returned status.
asynchronousBoundary.readVisibility: Reads after an emit must poll; the emitted transaction is not immediately visible.

refusalAuditRequirement: Every refusal must be stored or returned in an auditable result. A refusal that leaves no observable artifact is a contract violation.

coreRefusalPersistence.decision: Core stores AND returns refusal outcomes. Return-only is insufficient.
coreRefusalPersistence.why: The asynchronous boundary means the Adapter emits, Core executes later, and the Adapter may never observe the return value.
coreRefusalPersistence.noFullPayloads: Core must NOT persist full receipt or evidence payloads. Identifiers and hashes only, for privacy and storage discipline.

storageGrowthRule.note: The Adapter retains richer receipt/proposal history. Core needs only the minimum consequence audit record.

coreRefusalPersistence.contractViolation: A refusal that leaves no artifact is a contract violation.
